Area.evidence_source: Dan was described by his father, and others who knew him before he went to university, as a high achiever. ... He became much more "closed" and "introverted." His academic progress was irregular and at the end of his first year he failed two of his exams. Suffering from depression he re-sat these exams but failed again. ... The first early indication of Dan's perfectionistic thinking was hinted at by one of his friends... his own high expectations and heightened self-criticism distinguished him from his friends. ... diagnosed him as suffering from depression (with suicidal ideation)... it revolves really around being very critical of himself, never thinking it would come to this kind of thing. ... one of his friends attributed the onset of Dan's depression to academic over-striving and his intense need to avoid failure. ... the role that Dan's sensitivity toward failure played in his suicide. ... just feel like a failure. ... his worst thing was failure, he hated failure, and I suppose failing his first year at Uni was obviously a massive trigger. ... The letter he left said he felt like a black cloud hanging over his family and friends. ... In the event of failure his self-criticism and perfectionism seemed to predispose him to levels of depression (and the potential for suicide). Dan's suicide note conveyed a sense of profound personal failure; a feeling that he had let everyone down and a belief that he had failed to meet the expectations of the people who mattered most.
